Better neural noise calibration: what improved, and which uncertainty is validated?

114 sparse-view fits: 36 paired reruns plus 78 fits on 39 new independent motions. All models use marginalized external forces and the same six-view moving-camera schedule. Prediction-set coverage is conditional synthetic evidence. The Bayesian posterior audit fails; force/material posterior uncertainty remains unvalidated. Network calibration, prediction coverage and posterior exploration are separate checks.

Paired stochastic-case gap errors: independent floor 4.847 mm; previous neural 2.974 mm; recalibrated constant 3.281 mm; recalibrated neural 3.623 mm. Three underlying seeds are shared across conditions. These averages do not prove a neural-specific advantage.

1. Calibration now matches the operating regime

The same 33-parameter network uses scaled smooth magnitudes of strain and relative speed, encoding the declared sign symmetry. Twelve independent training motions vary mechanics and initial conditions; four other motions validate it. Operating-region and broad feature states receive equal mass. Training minimizes Gaussian innovation NLL from 128 independent synthetic innovations per state; analytic amplitudes are evaluation labels, not regression targets. The constant control is fitted directly to training innovations, avoiding inherited network bias. Weights are frozen before every reconstruction.

On independent calibration-validation motions: relative amplitude RMSE 0.281%, standardized innovation variance 1.009, and nominal-90% innovation coverage 89.85%. On the unchanged benchmark states, amplitude error fell from 36.29% to 0.295%. On the 20 fresh held-out motion sequences, pooled frame-state amplitude error is 0.295%. Synthetic simulator supervision is still required; weights are not learned from test RGB and weight uncertainty is not propagated.

3. Held-out validation of whole-gap prediction sets

Nineteen independent stochastic motions calibrate a maximum standardized position-error score; twenty new motions test it. Each case independently draws pulse/no-pulse with probability 1/2. A complete seven-frame gap (84 xyz components) supplies one score. Frozen model-specific multipliers use the 18th of 19 calibration scores. Calibration completes before any test fitting; test truths never adjust the network or interval multiplier.

Raw local 90% intervals are component-wise. Conformal sets target simultaneous 90% coverage of the entire missing-motion gap, a stricter event. Their finite-sample marginal property assumes exchangeability of calibration and new motions and averages over calibration-set randomness. It is not a guarantee for every individual video, a Bayesian posterior correction, or evidence for another scene/view schedule. Twenty trials leave substantial statistical uncertainty.

4. Nonlinear posterior uncertainty remains a separate question

The neural pulse-plus-stochastic seed-4101 mode was refined. Its exact observed Hessian was assembled using local automatic differentiation, the force Schur complement and the complete force-volume determinant curvature. Independent dense AD on a smaller model and full-target Hessian-vector derivatives check the assembly. The maximum refined directional finite-difference error is 3.5e-05. Importance screens compare Fisher and observed-Hessian Gaussians using 512 draws each. Four Metropolis-corrected pCN chains target the full nonlinear marginalized-force density, with 1,000 warmup and 2,000 retained steps each. All 1,448 state coordinates, 84 gap components, target density and 15 conditional force means are monitored.

Posterior status: not_validated. 1548/1548 quantities fail the complete Rhat/ESS/frozen-chain screen. Even a finite diagnostic pass cannot exclude unvisited modes. Conformal prediction coverage does not validate the Bayesian posterior, material intervals, or force intervals.

Approximate local force intervals are separately scored on all test motions: Calibrated constant mean force-component coverage 96.3%, width 0.0746 N; Calibrated neural mean force-component coverage 91.5%, width 0.0741 N. These are correlated component averages, not independent force-trajectory coverage guarantees. They remain approximate.

5. Numerical checks, reproducibility and limits

Cross-runtime recovery caught a tied-eigenspace bug in the initial CI study: truncating the cube kernel to three modes selected different noise covariance projections on Windows and Linux. The final study freezes the projection already published with v0.7. The initial 19/20 coverage result is superseded diagnostic evidence. Final test seeds 83001–83020 are fresh. No network retraining or hyperparameter tuning followed the initial test results.

A separate empty-depth-slab audit found incorrect emission derivatives at zero density. The corrected renderer evaluates the analytic zero-density emission limit, and tests its first and second derivatives against the closed-form single-color solution. Every final comparison and validation fit uses both fixes. Earlier v0.7 versus final results therefore include calibration and numerical changes; neural versus constant within the final run is the controlled noise-model comparison.

All stochastic evaluation motions use independent coupled 192/384/768-grid references, balance/support checks, and an oracle-amplitude production 6/12-step consistency audit. Deterministic motion retains the converged RK4-96 reference. Exact observed RGB is unchanged for the 36 paired fits. These are numerical consistency checks, not absolute SDE/mesh/experimental error bounds.

Known eight-node/six-tetrahedron mesh, 30 Gaussians, known appearance/cameras/density/supports, restricted external-force profile, retained independent discrepancy floor, and one sparse schedule. There is no real-video, unknown-geometry/camera or distribution-shift validation. Neither calibrated innovations nor finite-case predictive coverage establishes general physical realism.

The publication includes exact observed pixels, reference states/audits, every fitted solver coordinate, network weights, frozen quantiles, per-case force distributions/scores, all inference flags, CSV and source/artifact hashes. Large precision matrices and full raw chains can be regenerated from the committed source, inputs and seeds. Read docs/CALIBRATED_NOISE_PROTOCOL.md and docs/CALIBRATED_NOISE_RESULTS.md for equations, assumptions and commands.
